title: Next-token sampler
description: Move temperature, top K and top P over a toy list of next words and watch the same prompt give predictable or varied answers.
intro: A language model writes one token at a time. For each step it gives every possible next token a chance, then picks one. Inference parameters change how it picks. Start with the support answer and generate a few completions at temperature 1, then at 0, then at 2.
takeaways: Lower temperature means more consistent, focused answers: the classic exam answer for "more deterministic". Raise it for creative variety, such as slogans.
Top K keeps only the K likeliest tokens; top P keeps the likeliest tokens whose chances add up to P. Lowering either one also narrows the choice.
The same prompt can give different answers each run (nondeterminism). A low temperature reduces this but does not make GenAI right for work that must give identical results every time.
At a high temperature, unlikely and wrong words such as a 90-day return window get picked: randomness can look like a hallucination. Ground factual answers in your documents too.
Response length (maximum tokens) limits how long an answer is, and so its cost, not how random it is.
